en.title: Rotate a Square Matrix Ninety Degrees Clockwise
en.description:
Rotate the given square matrix 90 degrees clockwise and output the rotated matrix; the direction is determined by the original example and cannot be changed to counterclockwise.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The input is N M with N=M required, followed by N lines of M integers each. The original bounds only require a square matrix and give no numeric bounds; this site publicly adds 1≤N=M≤1000 and elements in −10^9..10^9.
en.output: Output the rotated matrix as N lines, each with N space-separated integers; do not output the dimensions again.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3 1 / 4 2; 7; 7 4 1 / 8 5 2 / 9 6 3. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Row c of the new matrix is column c of the original matrix read from bottom to top. Store the original matrix compactly and generate the output row by row.
